verses.text: Jesus said to them, "I tell you for certain, some people standing here will not die before they see the kingdom of God come with power."
Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and John with him and led them up a high mountain, where they were all alone. There his appearance was changed in front of them.
His clothes became shining white, whiter than anyone in the world could ever wash them.
Then Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters, one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."
Peter did not really know what to say, because they were all so afraid.
Then a cloud came and covered them. A voice came from the cloud: "This is my Son, and I love him. Listen to him!"
Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them orders not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
So they kept the matter to themselves. But they asked each other what "rising from the dead" meant.
They asked him, "Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"
Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah does come first, and he puts everything right again. Then why is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be treated as nothing?
But I tell you, Elijah has already come. And people did to him everything they wanted, just as it is written about him."
When they came back to the other followers, they saw a large crowd around them. Some teachers of the law were arguing with them.
As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with wonder, and they ran to greet him.
"What are you arguing with them about?" Jesus asked.
A man in the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has an evil spirit that makes him unable to speak.

Whenever the spirit takes hold of him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth and becomes stiff. I asked your followers to drive out the spirit, but they could not do it."
Jesus answered, "You people who have no faith! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me."
So they brought him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it straight away threw the boy into a fit. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy's father, "How long has this been happening to him?" "Since he was a child," he answered.
"It has often thrown him into fire or water to kill him. But if you can do anything, please feel sorry for us and help us."
Jesus said to him, "'If you can'? Everything is possible for the one who believes."
Straight away the boy's father cried out with tears, "I do believe! Help me to believe more!"

Jesus saw that a crowd was running to see what was happening. So he gave a strict order to the evil spirit. "You spirit that makes him deaf and unable to speak," he said, "I command you, come out of him and never go into him again!"
The spirit screamed and shook the boy violently. Then it came out of him. The boy looked so much like a dead body that many people said, "He is dead."
But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and the boy stood up.
After Jesus had gone indoors, his followers asked him in private, "Why could we not drive out the spirit?"
He replied, "This kind can only come out by prayer and fasting."
They left that place and passed through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know where they were,
because he was teaching his followers. He said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be handed over to people who will kill him. Three days after he is killed, he will rise again."
But they did not understand what he meant, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
They came to Capernaum. When Jesus was in the house, he asked them, "What were you arguing about on the road?"
But they kept quiet, because on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the most important.
Jesus sat down and called the twelve to him. He said, "Anyone who wants to be first must be the last of all, and the servant of all."
He took a little child and had the child stand among them. Then he took the child in his arms and said to them,
"Anyone who welcomes one of these little children in my name welcomes me. And anyone who welcomes me does not welcome only me. They also welcome the one who sent me."
John said to him, "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We told him to stop, because he was not one of us."
"Do not stop him," Jesus said. "No one who does a miracle in my name can soon after say anything bad about me.
Anyone who is not against us is for us.
I tell you for certain, anyone who gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to the Christ will certainly be rewarded.
"If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a large millstone tied around their neck.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life with one hand than to go into hell with two hands, where the fire never goes out.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life with one foot than to have two feet and be thrown into hell, where the fire never goes out.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
If your eye causes you to sin, pull it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
In hell 'the worms that eat them do not die, and the fire is never put out.'
Everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good. But if it loses its saltiness, how can you make it salty again? Have salt among yourselves, and live in peace with each other."
